title: A picked arrow's Appearance starts with its Arrow row, as the approved prototype draws it
goal: The arrow and measurement panel the user approved on 2026-10-31 opens with the arrow's own choices: Arrow, Chip, Color, Marker, Size. The shipped panel puts Opacity, Blending and Masked by on top, so the first three rows of a picked arrow are ones every layer has, and the choices the prototype leads with sit below them.
notes: Found by the digest on 2026-11-01 in the runner's own side by side, queue/audits/2026-11-01-markup-appearance-vs-proto.png: the prototype column starts at Arrow; the shipped column starts Opacity, Blending, Masked by, then Arrow. Same in 2026-10-31-five-arrow-styles-6-every-new-style-sc.png. docs/design/markup.md section 8 lists Appearance as Arrow, Chip, Color, Marker, Size, Advanced, with no Opacity, Blending or Masked by. The task that shipped it (arrow-and-measurement-appearance-shows-only-styl, eac717d7) closed with the side by side in its audit but did not mention the difference. Decide where the three shared rows go for a picked arrow or measurement (under Advanced is the obvious place, since markup.md calls everything else there; Photoshop keeps opacity and blending on the Layers panel, not in the shape's properties) and log the choice; a card only if it is a costly call.
acceptance: A picked arrow's Appearance reads Arrow, Chip, Color, Marker, Size, then the closed Advanced, with nothing above Arrow; a picked measurement the same without Arrow
Opacity, Blending and Masked by are still reachable for an arrow or measurement, and where they went is written in markup.md section 8 and in this task's log
Other layer kinds keep their panel exactly as before
A new side by side with the prototype is in the audit, and the shipped column starts at Arrow
